planned_decisions.rationale: Stacks now proves the directed extension-by-zero presentation of supported invariant sections for abelian G-sheaves. Its derived colimit comparison is asserted only under the separately stated Gamma_X^G-acyclicity condition for extension by zero, and its ordinary supported-cohomology comparison additionally assumes that Phi is paracompactifying; neither extra condition is inferred from the neighbourhood hypothesis.

Stacks now constructs the additive first-quadrant filtered second spectral sequence for abelian G-sheaves, with the displayed colimit E_2-page and finite abutment filtration. The abutment identification uses the explicit extension-by-zero acyclicity condition; the usual H^p(G,H^q_Phi) page additionally requires Phi to be paracompactifying and one of the three alternative interchange criteria.

Stacks now constructs the compatible directed system from the E_2-pages onward, takes exact filtered colimits pagewise, proves stabilization and finite convergence, and identifies the abutment through the preceding conditional extension-by-zero comparison. It does not assert an unconditional second Grothendieck spectral sequence.

Stacks now proves the comparison colim_U H^p(G,M_U^q) to H^p(G,colim_U M_U^q) under each of the source's three alternative criteria: finite G; trivial actions with every H_r(G,Z) finitely generated; or an essentially constant cofinal subsystem. The resulting usual E_2-page still assumes that Phi is paracompactifying and retains the standing extension-by-zero acyclicity hypothesis.

planned_issue_append.claim: The p. 220 passage passes from the degree-zero supported-section colimit to the derived formula (5.7.6) under only the neighbourhood condition on Psi, and later identifies colim_U H^q(X,A_U) with H^q_Phi(X,A). The first derived identification additionally requires Gamma_X^G-acyclicity of extension by zero on injective G-sheaves, while the ordinary supported-cohomology identification requires Phi to be paracompactifying; the three subsequent group-cohomology criteria supply neither hypothesis.

classification_reason: The two D1010 lemmas formalize the p. 220 filtered extension-by-zero and second-spectral-sequence block for abelian G-sheaves. The first separates the degree-zero consequence of the neighbourhood hypothesis from the additional extension-by-zero acyclicity and paracompactifying gates. The second constructs the compatible filtered spectral sequence and proves the three source criteria as alternative conditions only for group-cohomology/filtered-colimit interchange. At exactly this conditional scope, the four previously gap-classified units become existing_equivalent.
nonclaims: D1010 is restricted to abelian G-sheaves and makes no module-valued extension over a general equivariant sheaf of rings.
The neighbourhood hypothesis on Psi proves the degree-zero supported-section colimit but does not by itself imply the derived formula (5.7.6).
Exactness of extension by zero does not by itself imply Gamma_X^G-acyclicity of the extension-by-zero terms of an injective G-sheaf.
The derived identification colim_U H^n(X;G,A_U)=H^n_Phi(X;G,A) is claimed only under the explicit extension-by-zero acyclicity hypothesis.
The ordinary identification colim_U H^q(X,A_U)=H^q_Phi(X,A), and hence the usual E_2-page H^p(G,H^q_Phi(X,A)), is claimed only when Phi is paracompactifying.

The finite-group, trivial-action plus finitely generated group-homology, and essentially-constant-system conditions are alternative sufficient criteria only for commuting group cohomology with the filtered colimit; none supplies extension-by-zero acyclicity or paracompactifying supports.
The essentially constant criterion is asserted separately for each q on a cofinal subsystem and is not a claim that the original sheaf system is constant.
Functoriality of the filtered second spectral sequence is claimed from the E_2-page onward, not from an unconstructed E_1-page.
